items.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Isn’t that what Cab told Dizzy? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah.

ctx.x: so when I moved up from third trombone to second trombone, when he left — I never did play first trombone in that band — I learned a lot from Vinnie Forchetti, who was playing first trombone in that band for the last part of the time I was on it. I learned a lot from him. But I had one guy in back of me who loved me dearly, he was kind of a jokester, his name was Buddy Hanna and everything else, and he played kind of like Sweets Edison you know and stuff like that. But he’d yell down at me and says, “Stop playing…
Isn’t that what Cab told Dizzy?
